title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-lee
content:
Quick breadcrumb dump for the regional-failover + fallback behavior observed Nov 7-9. Mostly notes-to-self + commands tried. Not polished.

SUMMARY
- Incident: sudden spike of 503/504s for hosted-api customers routed to us-east1 around 2024-11-07T15:10Z. Automatic fallback to eu-west1 kicked in but some requests still failed with 503.
- Visible from logs: rapid drop in healthy backend count for model-group redwood/open-7b-instruct-q8 in us-east1; healthchecks succeeded but connection resets + backend process OOM-ish traces.
- Hypothesis: routing policy allowed fallback but mapping logic picked incompatible model variant (q8 vs q4_0) causing binary mismatch / runtime kernel errors on some nodes; second hypothesis is KV cache pressure and bursty prefix loads causing eviction storms and high latency leading to LB timeouts.

TIMELINE (local times UTC)
- 2024-11-07T15:08:12Z -- first 504 spike reported by synthetic canaries (latency > 10s).
- 2024-11-07T15:09:05Z -- SRE alert: Backend pool count down from 12 -> 3 in us-east1 for model-group redwood/open-7b-instruct-q8.
- 2024-11-07T15:10:30Z -- Smart-routing policy triggered fallback to eu-west1 (per policy: prefer latency, fallback to region with >5 healthy nodes).
- 2024-11-07T15:11:00Z -- Some requests returned 503 with "service_unavailable: No healthy backends" even after fallback.
- 2024-11-07T15:15:00Z -- Rolled temporary policy: prefer-dedicated-tier -> enabled (aim: force routing to Dedicated pool). Reduced errors but not fully resolved.

WHAT I REPRODUCED LOCALLY / COMMANDS TRIED
- Hit the same model from us-east1 and forced route: curl -> 504.

Commands (from debugging host in us-east1):
- curl reproducer (simple):
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -d '{"input":"hello"}' \n    https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/servers/redwood/open-7b-instruct-q8/generate
  -> got HTTP/1.1 504 after 11s

- List backends and health: (internal tool)
  ./rb-lbctl --region us-east1 list-backends --model-group redwood/open-7b-instruct-q8
  OUTPUT (snip):
    backend-12 (ip 10.2.3.12) status=healthy conn=3 rtt=80ms last-check=15:09:48
    backend-14 status=unhealthy last-failure=15:09:52 reason=reset_by_peer
    backend-20 status=unhealthy last-failure=15:09:50 reason=oom-kernel

- Fetch runtime logs for backend-20:
  ssh svc@10.2.3.20 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200'
  -> saw repeated kernel OOM killer lines around 15:09:49 for process redwood-infer-worker (pid 4681), memory spike, then segfault in runtime_shared_lib: "invalid read in matmul_kern.c: line 342"

- Check model-variant mapping table used by router at rollout-time:
  redis-cli -h router-cache get model_mapping:redwood/open-7b-instruct-q8
  -> returns 'variant:q8-2024-10-21, compatible_kernels:v1.3'
  But dedicated pool nodes log show they expect compat 'v1.2' causing minor kernel symbol mismatch warnings at load. (suspicious)

- Captured LB forwarding logs for a failed request that returned 503 after fallback:
  {
    timestamp: 2024-11-07T15:10:58Z,
    route_decision: fallback->eu-west1,
    target_backend: eu-west1-backend-7,
    backend_response: HTTP/1.1 503,
    backend_body: "service_unavailable: No healthy backends",
    note: "selected backend pool reported 0 available processes"
  }

SNIPPETS / ERRORS OBSERVED
- runtime logs (backend-20):
  [15:09:49] OOM killer invoked: process redwood-infer-worker (pid 4681)
  [15:09:49] Segmentation fault (core dumped) at runtime_shared_lib:matmul_kern.c:342
  [15:09:49] healthcheck: process exited unexpectedly

- router logs: 
  WARN router: model_variant_mismatch for request id=abc123 expected_kernels=v1.2 got v1.3; attempting fallback mapping
  ERROR router: no compatible backend found after applying fallback policy for model-group redwood/open-7b-instruct-q8

- LB logs: 
  2024-11-07T15:11:03Z GET /v1/servers/... 503 0.002s - "service_unavailable: No healthy backends"

HYPOTHESES (ranked)
1) Variant mismatch + kernel incompatibility. Router allowed fallback to pool in eu-west1 that has a different compiled-kernel ABI (v1.3 vs v1.2). Some nodes crash when loading quantized kernels -> OOM/segfault. Explains segfaults in runtime and "model_variant_mismatch" router logs.
2) KV cache eviction storm. During the spike, prefix-based traffic increased (many near-identical prompts) causing cache thrashing and memory pressure -> OOM on some worker processes. Could explain high latency and backend restarts.
3) Autoscaler misconfiguration: autoscaler reduced process counts due to stale CPU metrics leading to transient 0-process pools and LB returning 503s even after fallback.
4) Networking blip between us-east1 <-> eu-west1 causing partial success (some requests reached eu-west1 fine, others timed out mid-hop). Less likely given segfault evidence.

QUICK CHECKS / WHAT HELPED DURING INCIDENT
- Temporarily forcing route to Dedicated pool (prefer-dedicated-tier) reduced error rate from 8% -> 1.2% within 6m. Suggests some hosting tiers had more stable kernel compat.
- Rolling restart of problematic backends in us-east1 (backend-20, backend-14) removed OOM events for 12m window.
- Disabled aggressive KV prefetching for 10m reduced memory pressure on one cluster and prevented immediate recurrence.

REPRO STEPS (next time)
- Reproduce using internal load generator hitting same model-group with heavy prefix reuse to surface KV eviction:
  ./loadgen --region us-east1 --model redwood/open-7b-instruct-q8 --qps 400 --prompt-file repeats.txt --duration 5m
- Toggle router mapping to force variant v1.2 -> see if crash stops.
- Bring a single new node with kernel ABI v1.2 into eu-west1 and run integration load to confirm variant mismatch hypothesis.

CONFIG/OBSERVABLES TO CHECK
- router-cache: model_mapping:* entries and timestamps
- node labels: kernel_abi, quant_backend_version on backend metadata
- LB pool sizes and process_count metrics (per-backend)
- runtime logs for segfault/OOM around events
- KV cache eviction_rate, hit_rate for prefix keys

ACTION ITEMS (next)
- [ ] Add a validation check in the router to reject fallback targets whose kernel_abi != request.expected_abi (ENG-ops short-term patch) - assigned to Marcus Liu.
- [ ] Add circuit-breaker to prevent fallback to pools reporting process_count=0 (Sana).
- [ ] Run audit of recent kernel ABI rollouts (who/when pushed v1.3) and add rollout note to Confluence (me).
- [ ] Improve observability: surface model_variant_mismatch as a metric and alert if >5/min for a model-group (SRE).

NOTES / THOUGHTS
- The router currently treats model-group compatibility loosely to maximize availability; this incident shows there is downside to allowing binary-incompatible fallbacks. We should consider adding compatibility levels or hard constraints for critical models.
- For now, prioritize a short-term guard (reject fallback when kernel_abi mismatch) then work towards a more graceful migration flow.

REFERENCES
- Slack thread with initial reports: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABCDEFG/p1712000000000000
- Related PR touching kernel ABI tagging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/518

Misc notes: saved core dumps at s3://redwood-inference-cores/2024-11-07/us-east1/backend-20-core.tar.gz

-- Lee
